concept: LST and SOL depeg and rate inversion risk
summary: Source-anchored research for LST and SOL depeg and rate inversion risk. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: In the mSOL episode the lending venues' oracle choice decided who was liquidated. Marginfi priced assets at market, using a one-hour exponential moving average per Solana Compass, and said its liquidations fairly reflected market operations. Solend priced mSOL off the SOL oracle and said it does not treat an LST depeg as a liquidation trigger. SolanaFloor is a Jito Network subsidiary, and Solana Compass labels its write-up AI-generated, so treat these details as secondary. (medium confidence)

A debt-side stablecoin depeg matters only if the venue marks it. Jupiter Lend values dollar-stablecoin debt (USDC, USDT, USDG, USDS, JupUSD, PYUSD) at exactly $1 with no price feed, so a stablecoin depeg neither triggers nor prevents liquidation there (EURC debt uses a EUR/USD feed). Kamino instead applies price bands that reject stablecoin prices outside an expected range. Collateral-side stablecoin depegs and rate inversion remain risks for stable loops. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Kamino borrow rates are variable and set by pool utilization, so a positive spread can flip negative during high-utilization periods with no action by the position holder. Kamino's worked example of a negative spread is 3x leverage, 6% collateral yield and 8% borrow rate. (medium confidence)

High-LTV eMode positions have a thin buffer against a depeg that is priced into collateral. Kamino's example: a 5% depeg leaves a buffer on a 75% LTV position but may immediately breach the liquidation threshold on a 95% LTV eMode position. Kamino also says a small adverse move in borrow rates has a proportionally larger effect on position health at high leverage. (medium confidence)

Solana's epoch-based native unstaking takes about 2 days (Sanctum says 2-3 days), which limits how fast arbitrage can close an LST discount. Sanctum also says the network caps deactivation at 25% of total staked SOL per epoch, so a mass exit can take longer. (medium confidence)

Stake-pool rate oracles are not dependency-free. Kamino reads the rate directly from each LST's on-chain stake pool account with no off-chain dependency or oracle delay. Jupiter Lend reads the same kind of rate but rejects it if the pool has not been updated in the current epoch or if a deposit or withdrawal fee exceeds 0.5%, and it limits market-feed age to 10 minutes for user operations and 2 hours for liquidations. Before relying on a venue in a stress, check what it does when the rate is rejected or stale. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Kamino states the Jito Market (SOL) has an interest-rate cap mechanism that bounds rate spikes for JitoSOL/SOL strategies. Kamino describes this as a deliberate limit on the primary risk of its highest-leverage LST product. This is a single vendor claim and the cap parameters were not verified. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

An LST/SOL loop has two separate failure modes. A depeg is a price event: the LST trades below its stake-pool value. A rate inversion is a carry event: the SOL borrow rate rises above the LST yield. Kamino's Multiply docs rate depeg risk 'Eliminated (stake oracle)' and borrow-rate risk 'Primary risk' for SOL LST strategies. Galaxy's July 2025 analysis of ETH loops shows the two modes feed each other: a borrow-rate spike forced unwinds, and the unwinds deepened the LST discount. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

When the rate curve cannot restore liquidity (market-wide stress when borrowers cannot repay, or deliberate utilization attacks), Kamino relies on daily caps, supply caps and auto-deleverage. Its Risk Council can unwind the largest leveraged positions after a 72-hour warning to protect solvency; Kamino says this has never been used. A looper should treat that as a forced-exit risk that is independent of the position's own health. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Kamino and Jupiter Lend both value LSTs at the stake-pool exchange rate rather than the DEX price. Kamino computes LST price = SOL_staked / LST_minted from the on-chain stake pool account. Jupiter Lend reads the stake pool's accounting rate for JupSOL, JitoSOL and mSOL. A temporary DEX discount therefore does not move LTV or trigger liquidation on these venues. (high confidence)

Kamino and Jupiter Lend both value LSTs at the stake-pool exchange rate, not the DEX price. Kamino computes LST price = SOL_staked / LST_minted and reads it from each LST's on-chain stake pool account, with no off-chain dependency. Jupiter Lend uses the SPL stake pool accounting rate for JupSOL, JitoSOL and similar tokens, and Marinade's accounting rate for mSOL. A temporary DEX discount therefore leaves LTV unchanged and triggers no liquidation on these venues. Jupiter adds that these rates 'can differ from the amount you would receive by selling or redeeming the token'. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Stake-rate pricing removes market-noise liquidations but not fundamental loss, and it assumes arbitrage will close the gap: buyers purchase the discounted LST, unstake it for SOL at the stake rate and keep the difference. If a staking-pool issue blocks unstaking and a depeg persists, the lending protocol can hold collateral valued above what the market will pay. Kamino says that scenario risks bad debt, with losses socialized among lenders of the affected market, and lists supply caps, per-LST risk review and stake-pool monitoring as mitigations. Jupiter Lend likewise warns that its contract-based rates can differ from what selling or redeeming the token would return. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Monitor the spread, not the headline APY. Kamino says to watch the yield spread continuously rather than the APY shown when a position opened, and its Liquidation Analysis Suite simulates time-to-liquidation under borrow-rate scenarios, finds break-even leverage and yield, and backtests past market events. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

In a Kamino Multiply LST loop, Net APY = Collateral Yield + Yield Spread x (Leverage - 1), where Yield Spread = collateral yield minus borrow rate. A negative spread grows more negative with leverage, and Kamino states there is no floor. (medium confidence)

Stress tests in the same study found that leverage staking amplifies cascading liquidations under a severe stETH devaluation. Liquidations and the leveraged users' own deleveraging add selling pressure on stETH, which deepens the devaluation and spreads liquidation to ordinary (non-leveraged) positions. Kamino's LST-oracle page describes the same loop for market-price oracles. (medium confidence)

Whether a market depeg liquidates a loop depends on the venue's oracle. Kamino prices Solana LSTs at the stake rate (SOL_staked / LST_minted), read from the on-chain stake pool account, so its docs say a JitoSOL DEX price of 0.95 SOL leaves positions valued at about 1.02 SOL unaffected. Jupiter Lend also prices JupSOL, JitoSOL and similar tokens by the SPL stake-pool accounting rate (mSOL by Marinade's rate, INF by the Infinity pool rate) and states that these rates 'are not market prices'. Kamino describes a market-price oracle as the cascade-prone alternative: every brief LST depeg would liquidate healthy positions, and the forced sales would deepen the depeg. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)
